segments.text: Hi.
Day three.
I'm going to be straight with you, the way I have been since the first day.
For a lot of people, this is the toughest stretch.
If you woke up tired, short-tempered, a bit tearful, or wondering why you ever started this, you're in very good company.
And if today feels fine, that happens too.
Take it.
You haven't missed a step.
Either way, I'm glad you opened this.
You opened it when it would have been easier not to.
So here's today's whole idea.
Lower the bar.
Today doesn't have to be a good day.
You don't have to be productive, or patient, or cheerful.
You don't have to feel grateful that you've stopped.
Today, the only job is to get to tonight without nicotine.
Everything else is extra.
If you get less done, that's fine.
If you're poor company, the people who care about you can cope with that for a few days.
If dinner is something simple, good.
Feeling restless, irritable, low, foggy or hungrier than usual is common right now.
It's temporary.
It's a sign your body is adjusting.
The gap that used to open every hour or two is running out of places to come from.
I'd like to remind you of something you did in the prep week.
There was a day when you imagined throwing everything away, right then, before you were ready.
You noticed what showed up in your body.
Some of it was close to panic.
You gave it a number.
You breathed with the ring.
And then you gave it a number again.
It came down.
Not because you fought it.
Because that's what these feelings do when you stay with them.
Today's feelings are bigger, and they're real.
But they're the same kind of thing.
Let's do a small version now.
Take a breath, in a way that feels comfortable for you.
Notice the hardest thing in your body right now.
The tiredness, the edge, the wanting.
Give it a number, from zero to ten.
You don't have to tell anyone.
Now just stay with it for a few breaths.
No fixing.
And check the number again.
Whatever it is now, you stayed.
That's the skill.
One practical thing for today.
Decide now what you'll do if it gets hard, so you don't have to decide in the moment.
Planning ahead in a simple if-then way, if this happens, then I'll do that, makes people more likely to follow through.
And if you're stuck for a "then", try moving.
Even a few minutes of movement, like a brisk walk or some stairs, can help a craving pass.
In a moment, your reasons will be on your screen.
The ones you wrote before any of this started.
Read them slowly, especially the one you chose as your main reason.
That person knew today was coming, and wanted this anyway.
Lower the bar, and step over it.
I'll see you tomorrow.
